 Social Security COLA increase to affect 388,000 Mainers in 2027 
 Monthly payments to rise about $75 starting in January 
 By Joy Hollowell Published : Oct. 19, 2026 at 4:23 PM EDT | Updated : seconds ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google MAINE — The Social Security Administration has released its cost-of-living adjustment, providing a 3.6% increase for 2027.
 Starting in January, Mainers will see about $75 more in their monthly Social Security payments or about $900 for the year.
 “The Social Security Cost of Living Adjustment, or COLA, is something that’s built into Social Security that makes sure that as inflation goes up, your Social Security payments can go up too,” explains Bill Sweeney, Senior Vice President of Government Affairs for AARP .
 How the increase compares
 Sweeney notes this is not the biggest COLA increase in recent years. That came in 2023 with an 8.7% raise. It is more than this year’s 2.8% adjustment.
 “It’s not a bonus, it’s not extra money” explains Sweeney. “It really is designed to keep up with the higher prices for everything that people are seeing, whether it’s heating fuel, or grocery prices or pharmacy prices.”
 About 388,000 Mainers are currently receiving Social Security benefits.
 “In the state of Maine, Social Security has lifted 106,000 people out of poverty every single year,” says Sweeney.
 Rising costs could offset increase
 However, University of Maine Finance Professor Pankaj Agrrawal cautions that the extra money coming in 2027 may not go as far as recipients would like.
 “Because of the slighter higher increase in medical costs, health care costs, it will actually be harder for people receiving Social Security benefits,” he says.
 National Retirement Security Month
 This is National Retirement Security Month. 
 Age 62 is the average age for retirement. However, many Generation X-ers are now realizing that may not be an option for a while.
 “These are folks who are really kind of the first generation who didn’t have a pension as part of their workplace,” says Sweeney. “This is the 401K generation, the folks who had to do all of their own savings for retirement. And what we know is that they’re going into retirement in a really bad spot.”
 Retirement age considerations
 The earliest age to begin collecting Social Security is 62. Recipients who begin at that age take a 30% cut every month for the rest of their life. Age 70 is the age to collect the maximum amount of money.
 Those wondering how much money they currently have in their Social Security account can click here and sign up for a personal account. There, users can see a yearly record of their earnings as well as estimated benefits.
